## §11 deliverables (by milestone)

### 0.1

engine scaffold, `RevocationEngine`, `Rule`/precedence model with the one-to-one tests, purity gate, BCV, POM assertions; `SymVerifier`, the reference walker and the §9.1 chain generator in `revokt-engine`'s test source set (they move to the published `revokt-testing` in 0.3); TBS/SCT parser (incl. `producerKeyable`, `notBefore`/`notAfter`) with the D7 corpus, the issuer corpus and the §9.2 differential parser oracle (0.1 gate: oracles 1, 2 uber, 3a/3b, 4, properties D1–D3, D5, D6, D8 (gated direction; D8 gap reported)); JSON tree; clubcard port (v3 + v4); the C2SP `index.bin` reader/writer and `GenerationFiles` (`KotlinRevocationEngine.prepare` needs them); the `revokt-engine` jvmMain `Rule → BasicReason` map; the §9.1 chain generator, `SymVerifier` and the reference walker (the walker fuzzer itself is 0.2, with the walker); oracle CI

### 0.2

a minimal `Revokt` (`build()`, a synchronous `start()` that builds one `CandidateIndex` over `platformTrust.anchors(platformTrust.defaultDelegate())`, loads the seed, runs the in-memory updater on the loader dispatcher and publishes the generation reference, `close()`; no readiness future, caches, factory lock, per-delegate instances or `state`; start diagnostics returned from `start()` as `List<PolicyDiagnostic>` until `state` exists); candidate index and walker per §5.1, PKIX fallback on both platforms, the §9.2 read fallback in the JVM binding, the walker-only harness, `Evaluator.evaluate` over that one index (decision steps 2–3 and 5–8, walker reason reported directly; `Revokt.evaluate(…, delegate)` is 0.3); **the §9.1 walker fuzzer is built and runs against the implementation here (P1–P8 gate)** and the walker's adversarial review precedes it; Remote Settings protocol and content-signature verification with x5u path validation; CRLite updater and the updater record over `RevoktStorage.inMemory()` (the §6.5 key layout in memory; durability, `store.version`, pointer flip, crash recovery and the lock are 0.3); seeds with `seed.json`; data artifacts job; coverage sanity and rollback; the §9 data-path fixtures (a), (b), (d) and (g) less its `BLOCKED_BY_SELF` and `MIRROR` items; CI-only upki engine and the cross-engine suite (the issuer taken from the corpus chain's presented order, no walk needed); benchmarks

### 0.3

§6.5 store (`store.version`, `meta.json`, pointer flip, crash recovery, lock); C2SP bootstrap-only mirror and system cache; the §9 data-path fixtures (c), (e), (f), (h) and the (g) items deferred from 0.2; caches; per-delegate trust managers and `Revokt.evaluate(…, delegate)`; lifecycle state machine and readiness future; OkHttp and per-engine Ktor bindings; `OBSERVE` events, `status()` and `state`; Android instrumented suite including the null-host probe and the main-thread wiring probe under `StrictMode.detectDiskReads` on API 26/31/34/36, cold process and after a trust-store change (induced by `am broadcast -a android.security.STORE_CHANGED` as root on AOSP userdebug images, or by installing a user CA through `KeyChain.createInstallIntent()` under UiAutomator on images without root; the mirrored image matrix carries a userdebug variant for this); a consumer fixture built with AGP 8.5.2 that dexes the published artifacts (revision 38's Android floor; Appendix A); Baseline Profile and measured `AWAIT_DATA` (JVM default 2 s); WorkManager (`RevoktSyncWorker`, `Revokt.Provider`); system images mirrored into project storage for the emulator matrix; `revokt-testing`; optional `revokt-bc`
